svg.title: SC Neuromorphic Computing Systems — processes and interfaces
svg.desc: Intended process and artefact interfaces for all 56 programme entries. Neuromorphic development and general circuit engineering retain separate semantics, optional adapters and one traceable evidence chain. Feedback creates successor revisions. Arrows show architectural handoffs, not implemented dependencies or physical operating permission.

svg.text: SC NEUROMORPHIC COMPUTING SYSTEMS
Processes, interfaces and feedback · all 56 programme entries
Read left → right within each lane, then follow the evidence and optional production paths below.
ARCHITECTURAL HANDOFFS · IMPLEMENTATION AND QUALIFICATION TRACKED SEPARATELY
Solid arrows: intended artefact handoff. Dashed brown arrows: optional integration or revision feedback. Neither is a package-import graph.
SC-NEUROCORE exists as an integrated beta workbench. Extraction destinations and the general circuit platform retain their documented delivery gates.
Integrated workbench and planned specialised UI use the same versioned operations as headless clients.
Existing workbench; component extraction follows parent stability and separate acceptance.
Planned general design / review client; library and CLI retain the same operations. General
circuits can be used without an SNN runtime.
NEUROMORPHIC DEVELOPMENT
SC-NC names are planned ownership / extraction destinations; the current parent still integrates retained implementations.
MODEL & INPUTS
Numerical model, topology, encoded data and explicit
interchange semantics.
OUT: model graph + versioned streams
SIMULATE & LEARN
Accelerated execution and adaptation; experimental
models retain research status.
OUT: states + learned parameters + runs
LOWER & CHECK
Model-specific lowering, co-simulation and fidelity /
resilience checks. Rejection returns to the owning
revision.
OUT: implementation + check results
TARGET & ASSESS
Admitted target deployment, spike analysis and
workload-specific benchmark evidence.
OUT: target observations + comparisons
OPTIONAL CIRCUIT ADAPTERS
COMPILER / HARDWARE hand off explicit design views and target intent; no mandatory PDK or lab for simulation / learning.
GENERAL CIRCUIT ENGINEERING
Digital, analogue, mixed-signal and specialist views keep their own laws, units, models and acceptance criteria.
DESIGN & TECHNOLOGY
Design hierarchy / view correspondence; identified
devices, PDKs, libraries, decks and operation
compatibility.
OUT: design views + admitted profiles
DOMAIN OPERATIONS
Separate solvers, models and coupling laws.
OUT: simulation / synthesis artefacts
PHYSICAL & ASSEMBLY
Layout, extraction and physical checks; die / package /
interposer / PCB correspondence. Existing views can
enter here.
OUT: checked layout + assembly intent
BRING-UP & CHARACTERISE
DUT identity, instrument / calibration associations,
uncertainty and measured-versus-predicted results.
OUT: original observations + conditions
Dispatch admitted providers; propagate versioned artefacts; preserve failures, recovery and exact execution profiles.
All circuit stages: existing open-source tools first; optional commercial / own tools through explicit provider and technology contracts.
Local / cloud / cluster / future hosts use their admitted resources and data access. FLOW does not implement a physical control loop.
MEASUREMENT AND CONFORMANCE AT THE RELEVANT STAGE
Each group below contributes checks to the labelled operation; measurements keep their original source and applicability.
INPUTS & STREAMS
Applies to model / input and runtime ingestion: labelled
stimuli, encoding, conversion, codec cost / loss, policy
checks, replay and model lineage.
TO EVIDENCE: data identity + reports
NUMERICAL BEHAVIOUR
Applies to runtime / interchange: declared oracles,
arithmetic / randomness, test adequacy, NIR semantics
and classifier-confidence calibration.
TO EVIDENCE: scoped comparison results
IMPLEMENTATION & HARDWARE
Applies to builds / targets / lab: timing, bitstreams,
physical learning, links, reliability and
simulation-to-fabric divergence. Physical qualification
stays separate.
TO EVIDENCE: build / DUT / instrument pins
DEPLOYMENT & FIELD
Applies to admitted deployment: evidence-bound units,
baseline comparison, bounded incident histories and
explicit assurance gaps for human assessment.
TO EVIDENCE: deployment / incident history
ONE EVIDENCE CHAIN · DOMAIN RESULTS RETAIN THEIR ACTUAL OWNERS
Canonical bytes, hashes, sealing, signatures and validation contracts.
Queryable configuration / result lineage; preserve original inputs, failures and successor identities.
Shared benchmark-plan execution / result protocol; SC-NC-BENCH retains its domain workloads.
Aggregate requirement-specific circuit results; pass, fail and missing evidence stay distinguishable.
All operations contribute original results → manifests and lineage → scoped assessment. A valid record alone does not qualify a physical claim.
OPTIONAL MANUFACTURING AND EQUIPMENT PATH
Entered only with accepted design / technology / process evidence and the applicable supplier or site authority.
Approved routes / recipe versions, material genealogy, work orders,
inspections and controlled supplier handoff. Integrates the existing
manufacturing authority.
Equipment capabilities and qualified local execution-provider adapters;
instrument drivers have one source owner shared with LAB.
LOCAL CONTROLLER / SITE AUTHORITY
Retains real-time loops, arbitration, interlocks and protection. Actual equipment
state governs restart / lost-ack recovery; no blind physical replay.
MANUFACTURING INPUT
Checked design + approved technology + applicable acceptance + authorised route → supplier or admitted local process.
OBSERVATION RETURN
Material / inspection / equipment records → CIRCUIT-LAB and the evidence chain → measured-versus-predicted assessment.
FEEDBACK TO THE OWNING DESIGN / MODEL
Measurement, conformance failure or field incident creates a new attributable revision; originals remain immutable and comparable.
Data / numerical semantics, physical calibration and local actuation authority remain separate. Architecture does not imply released or qualified capability.
